baslik: The Foreman Who Lit a Fire to Escape a Fire
sonuc: overran a crew of smokejumpers in Montana
tetik: up-gulch winds pushing fire through dry grass
mekanizma: a fire on a steep grassy slope outrunning men who couldn't see it had spotted ahead
ders: the Forest Service redesigned training and safety measures
yanilgi: The survivor didn't outrun it. He lit his own fire and lay down in the burned ground.
tartisma: His crew didn't follow him into the burned patch. How do you trust an idea you've never seen?
basliklar: What Happened at Mann Gulch
The Escape Fire Nobody Followed
hook: He lit a fire to survive
sahneler: A crew of smokejumpers parachuted onto a wildfire in Montana.
Within hours the fire raced up the slope, and thirteen men were fatally burned.
They were heading downhill toward the river.
They couldn't see the fire had jumped ahead of them.
Wind and dry grass drove it uphill faster than they could run.
Their foreman lit an escape fire and lay down in the ashes.
The others didn't follow. He survived.
The Forest Service redesigned its training.

baslik: Firefighters Cutting Line Downhill Above a Fire
sonuc: trapped firefighters on Storm King Mountain
tetik: a cold front driving a surge in fire activity
mekanizma: a spot fire below crews building line downhill as winds rose
ders: the tragedy reshaped wildland firefighter safety rules
yanilgi: The fire was small for days. That made it look safe.
tartisma: A crew leader raised safety concerns about the downhill line. Why weren't they acted on?
basliklar: What Happened on Storm King Mountain
The Small Fire That Killed 14 Firefighters
sahneler: On Storm King Mountain in Colorado, a wildfire suddenly exploded uphill.
It overran firefighters, and fourteen of them were killed.
For days, the fire had burned only a few acres.
Crews built a fireline downhill from the ridge.
A jumper in charge raised safety concerns.
Red flag warnings had been issued.
A cold front arrived and the fire surged.
Wildland firefighter safety rules were reshaped.

baslik: The Hotshot Crew Trapped in a Box Canyon
tetik: a sudden wind shift cutting off their route
mekanizma: a weather shift intensifying the fire while terrain blocked the crew's view and radios faltered
ders: the tragedy prompted reviews of communication and situational awareness
yanilgi: Fire shelters were deployed, but the heat soared beyond what they could survive.
tartisma: Radio problems left the crew's position unclear. How do you track people you can't see?
basliklar: What Happened at Yarnell Hill
The Hotshots Trapped by a Wind Shift
soru: How do you track who you can't see?
sahneler: Near Yarnell, Arizona, a wildfire overran a crew of elite firefighters.
In minutes, nineteen members of the Granite Mountain Hotshots were killed.
Only one member of the crew survived.
He was serving as a lookout elsewhere.
A sudden wind shift turned the fire.
Terrain likely blocked their view of it.
Radio problems left their position unclear.
Their fire shelters couldn't withstand the heat.

baslik: A Controlled Burn That Burned a Town
sonuc: escaped and burned homes in Los Alamos
tetik: high winds during a prescribed burn
mekanizma: a planned burn to reduce fire risk escaping in drought and wind
ders: the National Park Service changed how it plans prescribed burns
yanilgi: It started as a safety measure. The burn was meant to reduce fire danger.
tartisma: Prescribed fire prevents bigger fires. How much risk should a prevention measure carry?
basliklar: How a Controlled Burn Destroyed Homes in Los Alamos
The Fire Set to Prevent Fire
soru: How much risk should prevention carry?
sahneler: A controlled burn in New Mexico escaped and raced toward Los Alamos.
Within days, the fire destroyed homes and labs, leaving hundreds of families homeless.
The burn was meant to reduce fire danger.
It was part of a hazard reduction plan.
Drought had dried the forest.
High winds pushed it out of control.
Over four hundred families lost their homes.
Prescribed burn planning was changed.

baslik: A Worn Hook on a Power Line Burned Down Paradise
sonuc: destroyed the town of Paradise, California
tetik: failed hardware on a poorly maintained transmission line
mekanizma: a worn line component failing in strong winds and igniting dry vegetation
ders: PG&E pleaded guilty to manslaughter and filed for bankruptcy
yanilgi: The fire didn't start from lightning. It began with failed hardware on a power line.
tartisma: The utility pleaded guilty to 84 counts of manslaughter. Should companies face criminal charges?
basliklar: What Really Started the Camp Fire
The Power Line That Burned Paradise
sahneler: Early one morning, a wildfire ignited near Paradise, California.
Within hours the town was mostly destroyed, and eighty five people died.
Hardware on a power transmission line had failed.
The line was poorly maintained.
Strong winds drove the fire into town.
More than eighteen thousand structures were destroyed.
The utility pleaded guilty to eighty four counts of manslaughter.
The century-old line needed manual effort to switch off.

baslik: The Sirens That Never Sounded in Lahaina
sonuc: destroyed the town of Lahaina on Maui
tetik: a downed power line igniting dry grass in high winds
mekanizma: wind-driven fire, failing hydrant pressure and no siren warning
ders: Maui faced scrutiny over warnings, water and grid safety
yanilgi: Hawaii had a huge siren network. It wasn't activated.
tartisma: A 2014 plan warned Lahaina was at extreme risk. Why do warnings stay on paper?
basliklar: Why Lahaina Burned So Fast
The Sirens That Stayed Silent
soru: Why do warnings stay on paper?
sahneler: Wind-driven fire swept through the historic town of Lahaina on Maui.
It destroyed most of the town and killed at least one hundred two people.
A downed power line sparked flames in dry grass.
Winds linked to a distant hurricane spread them fast.
Civil defense sirens were never activated.
Hydrant pressure failed as burning homes leaked water.
A plan had warned the area was at extreme risk.
Maui faced scrutiny over its warnings and water system.

baslik: The Deadliest Wildfire in History Burned the Same Night as Chicago
tetik: a cold front merging many land-clearing fires
mekanizma: slash-and-burn fires merging into a firestorm driven by strong winds
ders: the fire became a key case in understanding firestorms
yanilgi: It wasn't one fire. Many small clearing fires merged into one.
tartisma: It killed far more than Chicago but is barely remembered. Why do some disasters get forgotten?
basliklar: Why the Peshtigo Fire Was So Deadly
The Forgotten Fire That Killed Thousands
sahneler: On the night Chicago burned, a far deadlier fire swept Wisconsin.
It became a firestorm that killed well over a thousand people.
Settlers and railroads cleared forest with fire.
The weather had been unusually dry.
A cold front brought strong winds.
Many small fires merged into one.
It burned more than a million acres.
It's the deadliest wildfire in recorded history.

baslik: Scientists Were Convicted Over an Earthquake
tetik: an earthquake after reassurances days earlier
mekanizma: poorly built modern buildings failing in a known earthquake zone
ders: the trial sparked global debate on how scientists communicate risk
yanilgi: The scientists weren't convicted for failing to predict it. They were convicted for downplaying the risk.
tartisma: The verdict was later overturned. Should scientists face charges over risk messages?
basliklar: Why Scientists Were Convicted After L'Aquila
The Earthquake and the Reassurance
hook: They were told not to worry
sahneler: At night, an earthquake struck the Italian city of L'Aquila.
Buildings collapsed, and three hundred eight people were killed.
Six days earlier, officials had downplayed the risk.
Small tremors had been shaking the area.
Many modern buildings failed in a known quake zone.
Six scientists and an official were convicted of manslaughter.
The verdict was overturned in 2014.
It sparked debate on how risk should be communicated.

baslik: One Building Caused Most of an Earthquake's Deaths
mekanizma: an obsolete non-ductile concrete design failing under strong shaking
ders: a Royal Commission examined its design and approval
yanilgi: The building was inspected after earlier quakes and allowed to stay open.
tartisma: Its designer admitted it didn't meet his own standards. Who checks the engineers?
basliklar: Why the CTV Building Collapsed
The Building That Held Most of an Earthquake's Deaths
hook: One building. Most of the deaths
sahneler: When Christchurch was hit by an earthquake, the CTV Building collapsed.
It killed one hundred fifteen people inside, most of the quake's deaths.
It had been designed in the 1980s.
Its concrete frame used an obsolete non-ductile design.
Engineers inspected it after earlier quakes.
It was allowed to stay open.
Its consulting firm's head said it didn't meet his own standards.
A Royal Commission examined how it was approved.

baslik: The Dam That Nearly Failed Above 80,000 People
sonuc: nearly failed in the San Fernando earthquake
tetik: earthquake shaking liquefying the dam's fill
mekanizma: liquefaction of hydraulic fill causing a landslide that took part of the crest
ders: seismic safety of embankment dams was transformed
yanilgi: The dam didn't fail. The reservoir happened to be only half full.
tartisma: A full reservoir could have killed tens of thousands. How much luck is in every near miss?
basliklar: How the Van Norman Dam Nearly Failed
The Near Miss Above Los Angeles
soru: How much luck is in a near miss?
sahneler: An earthquake shook the dam holding Los Angeles' water.
Within seconds, part of its crest slid into the reservoir.
The dam was built with hydraulic fill.
Shaking made the fill liquefy.
Luckily, the reservoir was only about half full.
Eighty thousand people were evacuated for three days.
Engineers lowered the water as fast as possible.
It transformed the seismic safety of earthen dams.

baslik: A Tanker Fire Melted a Freeway Ramp
sonuc: had a ramp collapse after a tanker fire
tetik: a gasoline tanker overturning below the ramp
mekanizma: intense fuel fire weakening the steel structure above
ders: the collapse showed how vulnerable steel roadways are to fuel fires
yanilgi: No earthquake was needed. Heat alone weakened the steel.
tartisma: Steel is strong but weakens fast in fire. Should key ramps be fireproofed?
basliklar: Why the MacArthur Maze Collapsed
The Fire That Melted a Freeway
sahneler: Before dawn in Oakland, a tanker truck overturned on a freeway ramp.
It burst into flames, and the ramp above collapsed within minutes.
It was carrying eight thousand six hundred gallons of gasoline.
Fuel spilled and burned below the ramp.
The heat weakened the steel structure.
The steel above lost its strength.
A long section of the upper ramp fell.
It showed how quickly fire can defeat steel.

baslik: A Tanker Fire Under I-95 Brought Down the Highway
sonuc: collapsed after a tanker fire underneath
tetik: a gasoline tanker rolling over on an off-ramp
mekanizma: extreme heat from burning gasoline weakening the overpass
ders: a temporary roadway reopened the highway in under two weeks
yanilgi: It wasn't a structural flaw. Fire underneath was enough.
tartisma: Similar collapses happened in Oakland and Atlanta. Should fuel tankers be kept away from overpasses?
basliklar: Why I-95 Collapsed in Philadelphia
The Tanker Fire Under the Highway
sahneler: A tanker truck crashed and caught fire under Interstate 95 in Philadelphia.
Within minutes, the heat caused the northbound lanes to collapse.
The truck was carrying gasoline.
Its driver lost control on a curve.
The tank ruptured under the overpass.
The heat weakened the structure above.
It recalled similar collapses elsewhere.
A temporary road reopened I-95 in under two weeks.

baslik: A Gasoline Tanker Crashed Inside a Tunnel
sonuc: burned inside a tunnel near Oakland
tetik: a chain-reaction crash involving a gasoline tanker
mekanizma: a tanker striking a car, rupturing its trailer and igniting fuel in the bore
ders: hazardous cargo tankers were largely banned from the tunnel
yanilgi: Tunnel fires with flammable cargo are rare. This one showed why they're so deadly.
tartisma: Tankers were banned afterward. Should dangerous cargo ever share tunnels with cars?
basliklar: Why the Caldecott Tunnel Fire Was So Deadly
The Tanker Crash Inside a Tunnel
hook: A tanker burned in the tunnel
sahneler: Just after midnight, a gasoline tanker crashed inside the Caldecott Tunnel.
Fire filled the bore, and seven people died.
The double tanker drifted between lanes.
It struck a car.
The gasoline trailer was damaged.
Fuel ignited inside the tunnel.
Several vehicles were caught in the fire.
Tankers carrying hazardous cargo were largely banned from the tunnel.

baslik: The Crossing Crash That Turned Into a Train Fire
sonuc: saw a commuter train hit an SUV at a crossing
tetik: an SUV caught between descending gates
mekanizma: a collision that tore up the electrified third rail, which fed a fire in the lead car
ders: grade crossing and third-rail safety came under review
yanilgi: Most deaths weren't from the impact. The damaged third rail led to a deadly fire.
tartisma: Every crossing is a meeting point of road and rail. Should busy crossings exist at all?
basliklar: Why the Valhalla Train Crash Was So Deadly
The Third Rail That Fed a Fire
hook: The third rail fed the fire
sahneler: A Metro-North commuter train struck an SUV at a crossing near Valhalla, New York.
Fire broke out, and six people were killed.
The SUV was caught as the gates came down.
The driver moved forward onto the tracks.
The train hit it.
The collision tore up the electrified third rail.
The damaged rail led to a fire in the first car.
It was Metro-North's deadliest crash.

baslik: A Switch Left Set Toward a Parked Train During a Signal Outage
sonuc: sent an Amtrak train into a parked freight
tetik: a switch left lined toward a siding
mekanizma: a conductor's error during a signal suspension without other protection
ders: the NTSB faulted risk management during signal suspensions
yanilgi: Signals would normally have warned the Amtrak crew. They were switched off for work.
tartisma: One person's error had no backup. How should work zones be protected?
basliklar: Why Amtrak Crashed Into a Parked Train at Cayce
The Switch Left Wrong During a Signal Outage
soru: How should work zones be protected?
sahneler: Before dawn in South Carolina, an Amtrak train slammed into a parked freight train.
Two crew members were killed, and more than a hundred people were hurt.
Signals on the line were suspended for work.
A freight train had been moved onto a siding.
The switch wasn't returned to the main line.
The Amtrak train was diverted straight into it.
The NTSB blamed poor risk assessment and a conductor's error.
Work zone protection came under scrutiny.

baslik: The Engineer's Sleep Disorder Nobody Diagnosed
sonuc: sent a train through the end of the line at Hoboken
tetik: an engineer with undiagnosed sleep apnea
mekanizma: a train entering a terminal too fast and overrunning the bumper block
ders: sleep apnea screening for rail workers came under scrutiny
yanilgi: The engineer had passed his medical exam. His condition wasn't diagnosed until after.
tartisma: A screening program existed but missed him. How do you detect invisible fatigue?
basliklar: Why the Hoboken Train Crashed Into the Station
The Undiagnosed Sleep Disorder
hook: He had a hidden sleep disorder
sahneler: A New Jersey Transit train crashed through the end of the tracks at Hoboken.
It smashed into the concourse, and falling debris killed a woman.
The train entered the terminal too fast.
It went over the bumper block.
The engineer had severe sleep apnea.
It wasn't diagnosed until after the crash.
A medical exam had cleared him months before.
Sleep apnea screening came under scrutiny.

baslik: A Broken Sewer Undermined a Gas Pipe
tetik: a gas leak from a faulty pipe joint
mekanizma: faulty welds plus soil washed away by a leaking sewer, letting the pipe sag and crack
ders: the NTSB faulted both the gas utility and the city
yanilgi: The gas pipe didn't fail alone. A neglected sewer hole undermined it.
tartisma: The city rejected its share of blame. When two systems fail together, who pays?
basliklar: Why the East Harlem Buildings Exploded
The Sewer That Broke a Gas Pipe
hook: A sewer broke the gas pipe
soru: Who pays when two systems fail?
sahneler: A gas explosion levelled two buildings in East Harlem.
They collapsed in seconds, and eight people were killed.
A gas leak call came minutes before.
Crews arrived after the blast.
Two gas pipe welds were faulty.
A hole in a nearby sewer had washed away the soil beneath them.
The pipes sagged and cracked.
The NTSB faulted both the utility and the city.

baslik: The Rescue That Killed Three More
mekanizma: removing coal pillars that held up the roof, followed by further collapses
ders: the disaster led to scrutiny of retreat mining and rescue safety
yanilgi: The first collapse wasn't the end. Ten days later, rescuers died too.
tartisma: Rescuers entered the same unstable mine. When should a rescue stop?
basliklar: What Happened at Crandall Canyon
The Rescue That Became a Second Disaster
sahneler: A Utah coal mine collapsed, trapping six miners underground.
Ten days later, another collapse killed three rescue workers.
The mine used retreat mining.
Coal pillars holding up the roof were being removed.
Rescuers cleared rubble toward the trapped miners.
Another collapse struck them.
The six miners were never recovered.
Retreat mining and rescue safety came under scrutiny.
